caption: Oak bole foot at 10 h: plates now cut across into blocks by cracks, but in front sun the bark reads pale birch-grey, the crack ladder is too regular and the moss cushions still show a crackled-mud net.

Oak bole foot at 10 h front sun: bark now warm grey-brown instead of birch-white and the moss collar reads as soft olive cushions instead of a crackled-mud net; the cross cracks still look like short painted dashes and the bole is too smooth between them.

Same oak at 15 h against the light: the bole keeps a brown form in the shade with more bounce fill and the moss underfoot only shows a faint cushion pattern; bark detail is lost in the shade and the crown is still dark.

The carved Shrine of Binding lid on its worn two-step plinth in the ruined keep at dusk, sigil awake as the hero stands by; the whole lid face still hazes orange instead of only the cuts glowing, and the floor litter reads as a flat dark texture.

Oak bole at 5 m in 10 h sun: plate tops now carry fibrous grain and flakes that break up the sun on the bark; cross cracks still read as painted dashes, a pale lichen smear sits on the lit side and the moss floor still shows a cell net.

The Shrine of Binding lid at dusk with only the carved sigil cuts glowing ember on dark greystone, no more orange haze over the face; the keep floor litter still reads as a flat dark texture and the hero's face is lost in shade under the hat.

The ruined keep floor round the Shrine of Binding at dusk: warm beaten earth with gravel, sunk stone spalls, drifted oak leaves and tufts at the wall foot instead of a flat dark carpet; the leaves are still too even in size and a few white pebble specks pop.

Keep floor round the Shrine of Binding at dusk: warm dark beaten earth with big and small oak leaves heaped in drifts and dark twigs, the white pebble specks and stray daisies gone; the floor still reads a little too dark and flat in shade and the hero's face is lost under the hat.

The watchtower ruin from the approach in late-morning sun: ivy now climbs the keep's inner face in dark green mats seen through the breach; the outer face toward the camera is still bare and the near curtain blocks read a bit uniform.

Inside the keep over the Shrine of Binding: dense shingled ivy with lobed dark leaves and light young tips climbs the inner wall; the mats stand off the stone a little like shrubs, read too evenly saturated green, and the hero's face is still lost under the hat.

The watchtower ruin from the approach slope at 10:30: ivy now climbs the outer face either side of the breach toward the camera; it still reads as separate vertical strands rather than spreading mats, and the keep stonework is brick-regular.

Over the Shrine of Binding at 15:00: ivy leaves now lie pressed flatter to the inner wall with darker old leaves among them, but the pale young tips and yellowing leaves read like white flower specks, and the hero is a dark silhouette.

Watchtower ruin from the approach slope at 10:30: the ivy now spreads into a wide dark mat over the keep face instead of thin vertical strands, but the keep stonework is still brick-regular and blocky.

Over the Shrine of Binding at 15:00: ivy stems now fan sideways into branching mats and the white-speck young/yellow leaves are gone, but the mats still read as bushy fans on the wall, the stones are slab-like and the hero is a dark silhouette.

Watchtower ruin from the approach slope at 10:30: the keep and curtain are now coursed rubble masonry of mixed-length stones with staggered dark joints instead of brick rows, but the stone is flat cold grey and the low ring still reads as stacked slabs.

Over the Shrine of Binding at 15:00: the inner keep wall now shows mixed stones with chipped rounded arrises and open joints, but the floor rubble is pale and slab-like, colour is uniform grey and the hero is still a dark silhouette.
The keep from the approach: stones now vary by bed (warm buff, ochre, rust-stained, pale, dark grey) with shadowed joints; the low ring still reads as stacked slabs with pale top edges.
Inside the keep: warmer, per-stone varied masonry with dark open joints and soil in the low ones; plinth stones still slab-like and the hero a dark silhouette.

The keep from the approach: the exposed course tops now weather dark and mossy, with no pale edges, and the crest is ragged with slumped stones; the wall-top grass is still too small to read and the low ring looks like neat stacked courses.
Grass tufts now root along the broken crests of the keep and the low breach-side ring; that ring still reads as neat stacked courses instead of a tumbled scree of stone and soil.

Keep crest now steps up and down in ragged columns with talus at its foot; the neat low ring in front is actually the curtain wall, still stacked brick-regular courses, and the foreground grass hides the scree.
The ruined curtain wall in front of the keep now steps up in stone-wide columns over a talus in the grass; it still reads as a neat stepped stack of pale-edged slabs rather than a tumbled wall.

The curtain wall stub in front of the keep: its upper stones now sit out of true and grass sprouts from the low joints over a deeper talus; the courses still read as too regular and pale-edged at this range.
Curtain wall stub below the ruined keep now weathered dark grey with mossy caps instead of pale-edged slabs; courses still read as a regular grid and the keep crest is still pale-rimmed.
The hero at 22:30 under a moonlit sky with fireflies: the face fill is now cool and dim, but the face band still reads as a pale grey doll mask in a black hood, and the far ridges are faceted.

The hero at 22:30 by moonlight: the face now sinks into the hood's shadow under the brow, eye whites are grey instead of goggle-white and the hood rim reads; the hood opening still cuts the face as a hard polygon and the far ridges are faceted.

The hero at 10:30 in the meadow: the hood's face opening is now a rounded arch with a thick rolled hem instead of a straight-edged cut; the face still reads too bright and doll-like at noon with startled eyes, and a pale patch shows at the throat under the face cloth.

The hero's face at noon after the eyeballs were recessed: dark almond eyes under the lids and tanned skin in the hat's shade instead of goggle eyes on an orange doll face; still a hot specular dot in each eye, flat-looking wool on the hood and cloth, and a little pale armour at the collar.

The hero's hood and face cloth now read as heavy fulled wool with fibre fuzz, soft creases and folds hanging from the nose, the cloth tucked into the mantle collar so no pale armour shows, and the eyes carry a soft glint instead of a hot white dot; the face skin is still smooth and the face cloth's top edge is a straight cut.

The hero's hood now ends in a clean turned and stitched hem instead of a torn edge, and the face cloth rides up over the nose bridge and dips under the cheekbones; still wrong: the eyes look a little startled, the hood's front lappets hang as lumpy points and the skin is too smooth.

The hero's face at noon with relaxed upper lids over the irises, greyer shaded eye whites and a weathered skin grain with crow's feet and frown lines; still wrong: the outer eye whites read bright at this range and the hood's front lappets hang as lumpy points.

Hero portrait at 10:30: the eye whites now fall into shadow at the corners with a pink-brown inner corner, and the face edges sink into the hood; still wrong: lumpy hood lappets over the chest and a pale lit patch on the left brow.

Hero at 23:00 under the moon with fireflies: the face reads as dim warm-neutral skin instead of grey-lavender; still wrong: fireflies light nearby grass a hot yellow-green and the far left ridge is a flat pale cut-out.

The hero's hood now sweeps up in a rounded edge under the chin instead of hanging two lumpy points over the chest; still wrong: the face cloth's sagging tip shows below the hood and the eyes still read a little startled.

The hero's face cloth now ends tucked inside the hood instead of hanging a sagging point below it; still wrong: the hood's left side still falls in a long fold over the mantle and the eyes read a little startled.
Hero portrait at 10:30: the hood now ends in a short collar over the shoulders; the near side still reads as a narrow strip and the eyes look a little startled.
Hero portrait at 10:30: the hood now wraps round the sides of the face cloth instead of a thin strip beside it; eyes still a little startled and a pale patch on the left brow.

Night meadow with fireflies: their light now gives a soft warm-green glow instead of turning the grass and practice post hot lime. Still wrong: one hot yellow straw blade near camera, and the far ridges are pale flat cut-outs against the night sky.
Night meadow at 23:00: the far mountain ring now sinks into faint moonlit silhouettes instead of pale cut-outs; the meadow itself is still a flat grey-blue wash.
Night meadow at 23 h: moonlit grass tops now read cool silver over deep blue shadow instead of one grey wash; still too uniformly blue, the post's rope wrap stays yellow and the hero is a dark lump.

Dawn over the vale, where the first soundscape now plays a dawn chorus from the oak groves; the far peaks are still pale grey cones, too bright against the dark land, and the foreground grass is murky.
Morning sun raking across the meadow toward the oak grove, where birdsong and rook caws now sound; the far peaks still read as milky flat cut-outs, and the rooks are too small to see.

Late-afternoon squaring off with the Hollow by the practice post (the fight now has swishes, impacts and footfalls); still wrong: both fighters are near-black backlit silhouettes, the straw post reads as a smooth cartoon cylinder, the far peaks are pale grey.

Afternoon fight in back light: hero and Hollow now take meadow bounce and a sun rim, so the red robe, ochre sash, wraps and ash skin read instead of black cut-outs; the straw post is still a smooth cartoon cylinder and the far peaks are pale.

The practice post is now a bundle of loose straw stalks lashed with twisted rope, its cut ends splaying like a broom; the oak above and below it is still a near-black silhouette in back light with lime moss blotches.
Close-up of the straw bundle: individual gold, grey and rusty stalks, sagging rope lashings biting into the bulges; the oak post top still reads black and flat.

Practice post at 16:30 in back light: the oak now reads as silver-grey weathered wood with a pale end-grain cap and dark moss only at the foot, instead of a black cut-out; the iron band is still a flat black stripe and the far peaks are pale flat cones.

Morning over the vale: the far ring now rises as broad shouldered massifs that fade back in hazy layers instead of needle cones; the right-hand massif is still a milky flat wash in the haze and its faces lack forest/rock detail at this range.

The practice post's iron band now reads as rusty forged iron with hammer facets worn dull grey, two rivets and rust runs staining the oak below, instead of a flat black stripe; at this range the band is small and the far peaks still wash pale.

The far massifs now stand darker and bluer than the sky in layered haze with snow on the tops, instead of a milky wash; their faces are still flat grey with little forest or rock break-up at 1.5-2.5 km, and the mid-range trees are sparse.
Upper massifs now break into dark rock ribs with pale snow-filled couloirs; their lower flanks are still a flat grey-blue wash and the left peak's streaks swirl a little.

The far massifs' mid and lower flanks now break into dark dwarf-pine ribs, paler grass couloirs, cliff bands with scree and avalanche chutes through the forest, instead of one grey band; the break-up is still faint under the 2 km haze and the left peak's streaks swirl.

At night the far ring now stands as layered moonlit blue-grey massifs with faint snow tops in a haze a shade darker than the sky, instead of a pure black cut-out; the near volumetric haze band still glows brighter than the land round it.

At 18:50 the far ring is dimmer and its flanks sink into blue haze instead of glowing pale over a black valley; the moonlit snow tops still read bright and the left peaks' rib streaks swirl like marble.
The far ring by day: couloirs and ribs now run straight down the massif faces with no marble swirl, but the central massif reads a little like regular organ-pipe flutes and lost some summit snow.
The far ring at dusk: dimmer moonlit snow and no swirl, but the central massif shows regular pale vertical stripes.
Far massifs at 10:30: ribs and snow couloirs now wander, fork and vary in width with fuller summit snow instead of even organ-pipe flutes; the lower flanks still read as a flat haze band.

The far ring under a storm front: the massifs now sink to dark storm-grey silhouettes rising out of a low rain band instead of glowing pale cut-outs; their faces show no relief in the rain and the edges are a little crisp for 2 km of downpour.

Esc now pauses inside the ruined keep and opens a lacquer-and-brass sound panel (master, ambience, wildlife, effects, music); the sliders' grabbers are still Godot's stock white knobs and the dimmed keep behind is flat.
Pause panel with the new Picture section (quality preset Low..Ultra, FSR 2 render scale) lined up under the sound sliders over the keep interior; slider knobs are still stock white, not brass.

Hesper, the shrine keeper, tends the sealed lid in the ruined keep at 9 h in her own undyed wool, ash hood and faded woad robe; she still wears the hero's body cut and hat, and her linen leg wraps read too pale and thick.
Hesper gathering at an oak below the keep in the afternoon, side-on to the bole; she just stands (no stoop-and-pick animation) and the shaded oak bole reads glossy black.
Before dawn Hesper dozes seated against the keep's inner wall, knees drawn up and hat bowed over them; reads as a sleeper, but her old armour knee caps show orange and there is no bedroll or fire.

Speaking with Hesper under her gather oak: she stops and faces the hero and her line shows as a brass-and-bone subtitle; but she still wears the hero's cut, hat and armour plates, so the two read as twins, and the meadow light is flat.

Hesper gathering under an oak, side-on: no hat now, a hood, a woven willow basket of deadwood on her back and a slight stoop, so she no longer reads as a second hero; but her robe is two strips with wrapped legs between and the old armour shows at her side.
Before dawn in the keep, Hesper's basket of deadwood stands on the floor beside her as she dozes against the inner wall; the scene is very dark and she is a shapeless lump in the shadow.

Hesper on her afternoon meadow walk, basket on her back, standing among the grazing red deer below the keep; still wrong: the deer read small and flat-lit, the far oak savanna is thin and the noon light is flat.

Hesper crouched under a gather oak, reaching into the leaf litter with her basket of deadwood on her back; her hand still stops at knee height, the oak bole close up reads as shiny dark cloth, the litter has bright white flecks and the robe reads saturated blue.

Hesper side-on at a gather oak: her faded blue robe now closes into a bell skirt to the ground instead of two edge-on strips; still wrong: her back leg shows grey-wrapped behind the skirt in this stance and the frame is dark and flat.

Hesper crouched under an oak with her back bent and her hand down in the leaf litter, picking; still wrong: top-down framing, a tiled litter with white flecks, a saturated blue robe and a glossy black bole.

Hesper from behind at the gather oak, her right arm up at the basket to drop a find; the arm is hidden behind the basket, which hangs well off to her left, the leaf litter is a tiled pattern with white flecks and the oak bole reads glossy black.

Hesper crouched at the litter from the new low camera (3 m back, 0.6 m up): on this slope the frame tilts, grass blades sit in front of the lens and she reads as a dark heap; the litter still tiles with white flecks.

Hesper from behind under the gather oak with her shoulders squared and the willow basket on her back; still wrong: tiled leaf litter with white flecks, grey armour knee caps at her legs, glossy black oak bole, and her raised arm hidden behind the basket.

Under the gather oak the leaf litter no longer carries cream-white flecks or pale pebbles: darker russet and wet-brown leaves of mixed sizes with soft shadows under each; still reads as a mosaic of separate leaves, the bole is glossy black and Hesper's robe (shot taken before the slate-grey change) still navy.

The gather oak's bole in back light now reads as grey-brown plated bark with olive moss on its shaded side instead of a glossy black-green column with bright crack rims; the leaf litter still reads as a mosaic of pale separate leaves and the lower bole keeps one bright plate edge.

The leaf litter under the gather oak now lies in drifts of overlapping lobed leaves over dark leaf mould instead of an even polka-dot grid; the top tan leaves are still a greyish pale against too-dark mould, and Hesper's knee wraps show grey.

The oak leaf drifts now lie russet and warm tan over a brown leaf mould instead of greyish-pale leaves on near-black gaps; the bole's crack rims still read as carved lines and Hesper's body is still the hero's.

Hesper crouched in the leaf litter under a gather oak, seen from a level, low side camera with no grass blades in the lens; her body still reads as a dark jumble of robe and armour, the leaves are near-uniform blobs and a fern card glows too bright.

Hesper crouched at the gather oak: her body now reads as grey wool and linen instead of black lacquer and iron, robe lighter; still a busy bundle of separate panels and a lime back-lit fern on the left.

Hesper picking at the gather oak with the fern on the left now a deeper green with its own weaker backlight; the fern still glows against the sun, the pick camera tilts down with straw blades in the lens, and her crouched body is still a jumble of panels.
Hesper picking under an oak at 11:00: the fern against the sun no longer glows lime, but the low lens reads tilted on the slope and her crouched body is still a jumble of panels.

Hesper crouched at the litter under a gather oak: her robe now falls over her knees and hangs to the ground instead of jutting out with her pelvis; still wrong: the low lens sits on the slope so the frame reads tilted, and her crouched body is a dark bundle at 3 m.

Hesper picking under a gather oak with the pick lens re-aimed to the most level ground: the horizon and the vale beyond now read level instead of tilted; still wrong: an oak bole and root fill the left third and she is seen from behind as a grey bundle.

Hesper crouched at the litter against the oak and the ruined keep, lens kept clear of the boles: level frame, robe drapes to the leaves; still wrong: seen from above and behind, her crouch is a dark slate bundle and the litter leaves are all one size.

Hesper's new cookfire in the ruined keep at night: flames, firelight and soft shadows on the inner wall and ivy, sooted ring stones; still wrong: the lens sits in the wall-foot rubble so dark slabs fill the lower half, the fire is small in frame and Hesper dozing beside it reads as a dark blob.

Hesper kneeling at her cookfire at dusk just after it catches: the flame throws warm light and shadows up the ivied inner wall; still wrong: from the lid she reads as a basket blob with her back to the lens, the lid rim fills the lower third.

Hesper kneeling at the ring as the fire she just struck catches, basket now set down: the flames light the ivied keep wall well, but a fan of dark rubble slabs fills the lower half and she is still a dark shape beside the fire.

Hesper knelt at the tinder at dusk: the fire and its new ember glow light her robe and the ivied wall warmly and the ash ring is swept clear, but big floor slabs at the lens foot still fill the lower half and the flame core blows out to white.

Hesper's fresh cookfire at dusk from above: the flame is now orange instead of a white blow-out and the ash ring reads, but a row of big laid plinth blocks still fills the foreground and Hesper is an unlit silhouette right of the fire.

Hesper's young fire seen across the ring from beside the inner face: orange flames over charred logs, the ivied wall glowing warm, fireflies drifting -- but Hesper is hidden behind the flame and the ring stones read as pale puffy lumps.

Hesper's fire from the new low lens beside the ring: flatter, darker ring stones and the ivied inner face lit warm, but the lens sits too low and close, the stones still flare cream in the near firelight and Hesper is a dark hooded lump behind the logs.

Hesper's young fire from a raised lens on her side of the ring: the ring stones and ash no longer flare cream, but the inner-face blocks now glow flat orange under the higher fire light, Hesper still shows her back, and plinth slabs fill the lower right.

Hesper kindling her fire from a lower 1.25 m lens with warmer amber firelight: the flame and charred logs read, but the inner-face blocks behind it still glow flat cream (they want soot), she is a bowed hood, and plinth slabs fill the lower right.

Hesper's fire at night with the keep stones above it sooted (soot is near-black and matte now), but the fire light still blows the inner face out to flat orange right behind it -- the light is too strong at half a metre, not the stone colour.

Hesper's fire at night with a softer falloff: the inner face behind it no longer clips flat orange -- block relief, joints and ivy read in the firelight -- but the soot plume over the flame is still too faint and the plinth slabs fill the foreground.

Hesper's fire at night with the wider soot plume: the courses over the fire now go dark and the ivy, fireflies and keep relief read in warm light, but the stones right behind the flame still glow orange and the ash and logs flare pale.

The cold hearth at noon in the shaded keep: the wall over the ring is dark and sooted, but the cold logs and ash bed read bleached white-lilac, brighter than anything else in the keep -- not a material sheen (rougher char changed nothing), still to be found.

The cold hearth at noon after the keep fill on it was matched to the floor and the ash/split-wood albedo darkened: almost unchanged -- logs, ash and ring stones still read bleached white-lilac in the shaded keep, so the fill term was not the cause.

Diagnostic: the same view with the hearth's albedo forced to black -- the hearth goes black, so its white glare is diffuse light reaching it (suspect: sun leaking through a gap at the wall foot), not a sky reflection or specular.
Diagnostic: noon with the direct sun cut -- the cold hearth still glowed cream, so no sun leak; a second frame with the hearth's shade-fill term cut went near black, so the fill was the cause.

Noon in the keep after the fix: the cold fire ring now reads as dark sooted stones, charred logs and grey ash instead of a bleached cream star; the ash is a little cold blue-grey and the keep wall still reads dim and flat.

Dusk in the keep: Hesper's fire blazes in its ring and lights the sooted stones and ivied wall warm with no bleaching; the flame is still a simple bright tongue and the frame reads dark and murky away from it.
1 am: Hesper dozes beside her fire under moonlit lavender walls; the fire should have burned down low by now and its light reaches only a metre or two of the floor.
Noon in the keep: the cold fire ring's charred logs now read sooted warm-black instead of lavender, but the lens sits low in the wall-foot rubble and the shaded keep reads murky and flat.
1 am: Hesper's fire has burned down to a low flame on the embers while she dozes, but its light hardly reaches the walls and a big lime firefly blob floats near the lens.
Hesper's low fire at 1 am with no firefly blob on the lens; the firelight still barely reaches the moonlit inner face and the lid rim darkens the bottom of frame.

Hesper's low fire at 1 am after the night-grade fix: the keep's inner face now reads warm amber stone with relief instead of lavender-grey; the light is still a bit even across the whole wall for a low fire and the wall-joint grass glows gold.

The cookfire at full blaze at 22 h: warm firelit keep wall, ivy and swept floor with moonlit blue stones at the edge; the wall-joint grass blades flare as bright gold streaks and the lens is still a flat look at the wall.
The open meadow at 1 am back to moonlit silver-blue after the firelight grade had let straw-dry grass go olive-yellow; a few seed heads still catch a gold tint and no deer are in frame.
Hesper's low fire at 1 am: warm firelit stone, the light now dying off faster away from the ring; the wall-joint grass tufts still read straw-gold and the wall-on lens has no Hesper in it.

Hesper's fire at 10 pm: the wall-joint grass behind it is burnt off and singed, so no gold streaks flare on the sooted stone; the lit wall still reads too salmon-red and the ivy goes blue-grey under the night grade.

A red fox has come in out of the dark to sit just inside the keep's breach at 22:30, watching Hesper's fire; its white bib is a flat over-bright patch, the face lacks a readable muzzle and eyes, and the breach rubble reads as big pale slabs.

Hesper at 22:00 sat up by her fire, turned to it with hands out to the warmth, wall in warm amber stone; still wrong: the flame core blows out white, the charred logs show a regular crackle pattern and her near hand stays close to her chest.

The fox at the edge of Hesper's firelight after the look pass: red mask, longer narrower muzzle with dark sides, eyeshine, buff ear insides, only a narrow cream throat strip; still small in frame, legs and brush hidden behind the breach slab, fur reads smooth plastic.
Side lens on the sitting fox: head and chest profile read as a fox now, but a breach slab hides the body and the brush seems to stand up behind it instead of curling round the paws.

The fox at night bowed nose-down over the crust Hesper tossed it on the keep floor; the pose reads, but it stands on dark rubble slabs that hide its legs and the crust, and its coat is a flat saturated orange.
The fox sat on swept keep floor just in from the breach, whole body, forelegs and brush in view at last; still a flat saturated orange coat with smooth fur and wall stones lit like flat panels.
The fox at its crust spot on open floor, legs clear of the rubble now, but it stands head-up looking away, the crust is out of frame, the coat is flat orange and the legs thin sticks.

The fox stood at Hesper's crust at 22:30 on the new floor seat; still wrong: its head is buried in the breach rubble, the coat glows a flat saturated red with no fur breakup, and the firelit wall reads as salmon brick.

The fox nose-down at Hesper's crust on clear keep floor, head out of the plinth stones at last; still nearly head-on with eyeshine into the lens, a faceted low-poly body and a salmon-brick wall behind.

The fox sat at the edge of Hesper's firelight from the side with its new dense, sculpted body: smooth flanks and a round haunch instead of facets; still wrong: the brush sweeps up behind it instead of curling round the paws, and the keep wall reads salmon brick.

The fox at Hesper's crust with the smoother body mesh; still wrong: nearly head-on with bright eyeshine straight into the lens, the coat is a flat ginger with no guard-hair breakup, and the brick wall behind is salmon.
The sat fox's brush now lies on the turf and curls round its haunch toward the forepaws; the coat still reads smooth and flat-lit, and rubble slabs crowd the lens.
Side-on, the brush lies low along the ground behind the sat fox instead of sweeping up; the lens still sits high in rubble with a salmon brick wall behind.

Harrowmere's first cottage from the green in morning light: slate roof with eave moss, oak frame, limewashed daub, stone chimney; the chimney stones read as stark black/white blocks, the oak is flat grey, no smoke or path yet.

The cottage door bay close up: individually laid riven slates with lichen, hewn rafter tails, plank door with iron straps; the oak reads flat grey and the rafter tails are cut square to the slope instead of plumb.

The stone cottage (shot before it moved across the green to stand beside the timber house): rubble walls, slate roof, chimney with smoke, against the low sun; the walls read too regular and brick-like from here and the stones too rounded.
At the cottage door: rubble stones in lime pointing, tarred door, leaded window and graded slates; the shaded facade is flat, the eaves board reads ragged and the stones are still pillow-rounded.
At night the cottage windows glow warm through the leaded panes under the stars; part of the roof catches a pale moon sheen and nobody lives here yet.
The new dry-stone garth wall round the yard behind the stone cottage, late afternoon from beyond the back corner; rubble coursing and cope read, but the backlit foreground grass is flat and dark.

The garth wall's east gateway between two upright stoops at 11 h (first version); the face stones are too evenly coursed and pale with dark joints, so it reads a little brick-like (made more irregular after this shot).

The oak five-bar field gate hung shut between the garth wall's stoops behind the stone cottage at 11 h; still wrong: the oak reads pale silver-white and flat at this distance and the wall stones are pale blocks with flat moss tops.

Close on the field gate swung half open into the yard (it swings away from the hero and falls shut with a creak and a knock); still wrong: bars and brace read too pale and smooth, wall faces are light rectangular blocks, no track worn through the gateway.

From inside Harrowmere's new yard at noon: dry-stone walls with copes run from the timber house to the stone cottage, the cart gateway open between them; the stones lie in too-even brick-like rows, the moss is flat lime patches and the copes barely read.
Afternoon from outside the yard: the stone cottage and the wall top are backlit into near-black silhouettes and the wall vanishes in the shadowed grass.

From the yard side at 12.5 h: Harrowmere's dry-stone walls are now a cool grey gritstone with grey lichen, and moss only on the tops and shaded faces; still wrong: the garth wall's stones are rounded blocks in level rows and grass fills the foreground.

The field gate between its moss-capped stoops at noon, the garth wall now grey rather than cream; still wrong: the wall stones read as pale pillowed rectangles in brick-like rows, the cope tops carry flat lime moss and the cottage stones beside it are still cream.

Three of the garth's five hens (brown, buff, cuckoo) pottering on the scratched-short turf behind the stone cottage at 11:00; still wrong: the bare ground reads as dark straw streaks rather than dusty scratched earth, and the plumage is smooth with little feather breakup.
The same hens before the garth was scratched short: lost in knee-high meadow grass, which is why the yard now grows only a patchy short sward.

The hens' garth is now scratched down to dry bare earth with grit, dust-bath hollows and surviving tufts; still wrong: the claw-rake fans read as dark arrow marks (softened after this shot), the ground is flat grey-brown in the cottage's shade, and the cottage stones are still cream pillows.

The new oak hen house in the garth at 11 h with a hen climbing its ladder to the pop-hole; still wrong: boards read pale silver and flat, the nest box reads as a bare shelf, the garth dust shows smooth pale ovals.

The hen house after its look pass: creosote-brown boards worn silver on the grain, a tarred roof with a fascia edge, a proper nest box with a thick lid, and the dust baths now ragged patchy scrapes; still wrong: the garth sits in flat dull shade at 11 h, the dry-stone wall behind reads as dark even slabs, and the hen at the pop-hole is lost in the dark.

Stone cottage front at noon, now walled in grey split-stone coursed rubble on uneven beds with dressed quoins; still fails: stones read as rounded tiles with an even pale mortar outline, and the facade sits in flat shade.

Stone cottage front at noon after the rubble pass: stones now split polygons with deep shadowed joints and snecks instead of rounded tiles; still fails: cuts too deep so too much dark mortar shows between pale stones, and the facade sits in flat shade.

Stone cottage rubble after the cut/mortar tuning at 15.5 h: stones now fill their beds with narrower, lighter joints, but the facade is backlit in flat shade, the stones still read as rounded grey cobbles with pale tops, and the slate roof's lichen flecks read as noise.

Stone cottage door at 9.5 h after the rubble/slate pass: stones now vary in value and the slate lichen is in broad patches, but the wall stones still read as rounded blue-grey cobbles, the facade sits in sky-lit shade, and the lichen bands along the slate tails.

Stone cottage side wall at 9.5 h after the crisp-facet pass: rubble faces are now flat split planes with sharp arrises, but the stones still read as separate pale tiles on a wide dark mortar bed, the wall is still in shade, and the roof moss is bright green.
Stone cottage from the green at 15.5 h, backlit through haze with the yard walls in front: a believable farmstead silhouette, but the facade is flat shade and the place is empty of people.
